codebase.title: FISHPACK 4.1 separable elliptic PDE solvers
codebase.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA-256 over typed sorted regular-file paths+bytes and symlink paths+safe targets

agent_authored.description: FISHPACK 4.1 is a Fortran 77 library by Adams, Swarztrauber and Sweet (NCAR) of 19 subroutines that solve second- and fourth-order finite-difference approximations of separable elliptic partial differential equations: Helmholtz and Poisson equations in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates on centred and staggered grids, general separable equations (SEPELI, SEPX4), and the generalized block-tridiagonal and Poisson-type systems behind them (BLKTRI, GENBUN, POISTG, POIS3D), by cyclic reduction, with least-squares solutions of singular problems. It is vendored as its own codebase from the NCAR-Classic-Libraries-for-Geophysics container repository.
evidence: README.md and OVERVIEW of the upstream container repository
doc/README_* and the HTML manual under doc/

build.system: make (GNU make; one top-level Makefile per library, each including a make.inc that selects the compiler by `uname -s`; src/ builds a static library, test/ compiles and immediately runs every test program)
commands: make MAKE=make AR=ar F90="gfortran -fdefault-real-8 -O2 -std=legacy -J LIBDIR -I LIBDIR" CPP="gfortran -cpp -E"   (double precision, the darwin.dp reference build)
make MAKE=make AR=ar F90="gfortran -O2 -std=legacy -J LIBDIR -I LIBDIR" CPP="gfortran -cpp -E"   (single precision, the darwin.sp reference build)
pitfalls: make.inc chooses the compiler from `uname -s`: on Linux it wants pgf90 or g95, on Darwin gfortran but MAKE := the hard-coded gmake path, which does not exist on current macOS; override MAKE=make AR=ar F90=... on the make command line (all five libraries)

gfortran 15.2 (and every gfortran >= 10) refuses the Fortran 77 argument-type and rank mismatches in FFTPACK, FISHPACK and SPHEREPACK ("Type mismatch between actual argument ... REAL(8) vs COMPLEX(8)", "Rank mismatch in argument theta") unless -std=legacy (or -fallow-argument-mismatch) is given; measured: fftpack 12 errors, spherepack 2 errors without it

the shipped darwin.dp transcripts were produced with -fdefault-real-8; the libraries are written for single precision and the darwin.sp build reproduces fewer digits (FISHPACK 1 to 4 digits, MUDPACK 0 to 2) and mudpack tcud3cr does not converge in single precision (ierror -10 here, ierror -4 and NaN in the shipped darwin.sp)
wall_s is the double-precision `make` run, which includes the 19 test runs the test Makefile executes (under 2 s in total); the single-precision build took the same

pitfalls.symptom: make: pgf90/g95 not found (Linux) or the hard-coded gmake path not found (macOS)
pitfalls.workaround: make MAKE=make AR=ar F90="gfortran -fdefault-real-8 -O2 -std=legacy -J LIBDIR -I LIBDIR" CPP="gfortran -cpp -E"

pitfalls.symptom: gfortran >= 10: Error: Type mismatch between actual argument ... (REAL(8) vs COMPLEX(8)); Error: Rank mismatch in argument theta

every test program writes only to stdout; the test Makefile pattern rule runs each executable right after linking it (the pattern rule executes the program it just linked), so `make` in test/ is build plus run and output/darwin.dp is the whole transcript
pitfalls.workaround: run the .exe files again by hand to capture per-test stdout

modules.title: FISHPACK 4.1 separable elliptic PDE solvers
entrypoints: test/t*.f drivers, one per solver: blktri, cblktri, cmgnbn, genbun, hstcrt, hstcsp, hstcyl, hstplr, hstssp, hw3crt, hwscrt, hwscsp, hwscyl, hwsplr, hwsssp, pois3d, poistg, sepeli, sepx4
modules.expensive_path: cyclic reduction (blktri, genbun and gnbnaux, pois3d) and the FFT-based Helmholtz solves on the discretized grid; cost grows with the grid and the number of reduction levels
modules.rationale: The whole library is one module: one build (make, one static library), one test set, one scientific responsibility. FISHPACK 4.1 (Adams, Swarztrauber, Sweet, NCAR) solves second- and fourth-order finite-difference approximations of separable elliptic PDEs (Helmholtz, Poisson and general separable equations) in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates by cyclic reduction, with least-squares handling of singular problems and of coordinate singularities. It is vendored from the NCAR-Classic-Libraries-for-Geophysics container repository as its own codebase because the container holds five unrelated libraries that share no source; this one is packaged alone.
hazards: single precision by default; the darwin.dp references use -fdefault-real-8 and the single-precision build agrees to only 1 to 4 digits
FISHPACK90 in the same upstream repository is the same solver set behind a Fortran 90 interface (not vendored)
modules.purpose: The whole library is one module: one build (make, one static library), one test set, one scientific responsibility. FISHPACK 4.1 (Adams, Swarztrauber, Sweet, NCAR) solves second- and fourth-order finite-difference approximations of separable elliptic PDEs (Helmholtz, Poisson and general separable equations) in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates by cyclic reduction, with least-squares handling of singular problems and of coordinate singularities. It is vendored from the NCAR-Classic-Libraries-for-Geophysics container repository as its own codebase because the container holds five unrelated libraries that share no source; this one is packaged alone.
primary_inputs: grid bounds and counts, boundary-condition switches and boundary arrays, the Helmholtz constant, the right-hand side array F, a work array
primary_outputs: the solution overwriting F, a perturbation constant PERTRB for singular problems, an integer error flag IERROR
algorithm_stages: boundary-condition setup and right-hand-side modification per coordinate system (hw* and hst* front ends)
reduction to a block-tridiagonal or Poisson-type system
cyclic reduction (blktri/cblktri, genbun and gnbnaux, poistg) or FFT-based separation (pois3d with the bundled fftpack.f)
back substitution and singular-problem correction (sepaux, comf)
unique_responsibilities: direct solution of separable elliptic PDEs on regular grids
not_responsible_for: nonseparable problems (MUDPACK) and spectral operators on the sphere (SPHEREPACK)
evidence: src/ (the library), test/ (the drivers), Makefile and make.inc
runs.json: every driver built and run natively
